Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:10:1.hebrew: ונראה לר"י גירסת הספרים, דגרסינן: "א"ל אביי: אי סלקא דעתך דבעל לא ירית כו'", ולא גרסינן הכא "בין למ"ד בסיבת הבן בין למ"ד בסיבת הבעל", אלא גבי "אי אמרת בשלמא" דרב יימר בסמוך גרסינן ליה. ואמאי דאקשי רב פפא "דלמא קראי בסיבת הבן", מהדר אביי לשנויי הכי, וקאמר: אי אמרת בשלמא דבעל ירית, וקרא אסיבת הבעל קפיד — אתי שפיר הא דמשמע דאתי קרא למיעבד תקנתא אפילו לנחלת האם שלא תסוב, מדכתיב "ירושת שני מטות" גבי איסור הסבה. אע"פ שכבר הוסבה נחלת האם, מ"מ קפיד קרא שלא תסוב יותר על ידי נישואי הבת. ובסיבת הבעל איכא תקנתא, דמנסבין לה גברא דאבוהי משבטא דאבוה ואימיה משבטא דאימה, דהשתא לא מתעקר ע"י סיבת הבעל יותר ממה שהוסבה כבר. ואע"פ כשימות בעל ויירשנו בנו, מתעקרא נחלת האם משבטא דאימא לשבטא דאבא — שהרי הבן, אביו ואמו מתיחסים על שבט אביהן — או שמא הבעל לא יירשנה כלל, שתתאלמן או תתגרש, ויירשנה הבן — הא לא איכפת ליה, לפי שאי אפשר לעשות תקנה לדבר זה. אלא אי אמרת דבעל לא ירית, וקראי במסיבת הבן, כדקא פרכת — כי קא מינסבא נמי לגברא דאבוהי משבטא דאבוה ואימיה משבטא דאימה, מתעקרא נחלת האם על ידי הבן, כדפרי'. אלא ודאי בסיבת הבעל משתעי, ולהכי קים ליה לתנא דקרא דוכל בת יורשת נחלה בסיבת הבעל כתיב, מדכתיב ביה "ירושת שני מטות" — משמע דלנחלת האם נמי עבדינן תקנתא שלא תסוב יותר. והכי פירושא דברייתא: הרי הוא אומר "וכל בת יורשת נחלה", ובסיבת הבעל הכתוב מדבר, דמהניא תקנתא לנחלת האם. וכי תימא בסיבת הבן משתעי, וקרא לא אתא למעבד תקנתא אלא לנחלת האב — תא שמע: "לא תסוב נחלה", ומיתורא דקראי שמעינן דחד בסיבת הבן וחד בסיבת הבעל. ואם כן, ההוא דכתב ביה "ירושת שני מטות", דמשמע דבעי תקנתא לנחלת האם — בסיבת הבעל כתב, דאשכחינן ביה תקנתא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:10:1.english: It appears to R. Isaac (the Ri) that the reading in the books is as follows: that we read, "Abaye said to him: If it enters your mind that a husband does not inherit [his wife], etc." And we do not read here "both according to the one who says it refers to the transfer through the son and according to the one who says it refers to the transfer through the husband." Rather, [the phrase] "If you say, indeed" of Rav Yemar, [which comes] shortly afterward, is where we read it. As for what Rav Pappa challenged, "Perhaps the verses refer to a transfer through the son," Abaye turns back and answers it as follows, and says: If you say, indeed, that a husband inherits [his wife], and the verse is concerned about a transfer through the husband — it is well, [namely] that which implies that the verse comes to institute a remedy even for the mother's inheritance, that it should not be transferred, since it is written "the inheritance of two tribes" regarding the prohibition of transfer. Even though the mother's inheritance was already transferred, the verse is nevertheless concerned that it not be transferred further through the daughter's marriage. And in the case of a transfer through the husband there is a remedy, for we marry her to a man whose father is from her father's tribe and whose mother is from her mother's tribe, so that now no more is uprooted through the transfer by the husband than was already transferred. And although when the husband dies and his son inherits him, the mother's inheritance is uprooted from the mother's tribe to the father's tribe — for the son's father and mother are each attributed to their own father's tribe — or perhaps the husband will not inherit her at all, for she will be widowed or divorced and the son will inherit her — this does not concern [the Torah], since it is impossible to institute a remedy for this matter. But if you say that a husband does not inherit [his wife], and the verses refer to a transfer through the son, as you challenged — then even when she marries a man whose father is from her father's tribe and whose mother is from her mother's tribe, the mother's inheritance is uprooted through the son, as we explained. Rather, it must certainly be speaking of a transfer through the husband; and therefore the Tanna is certain that the verse "And every daughter who inherits an inheritance" is written regarding a transfer through the husband, since it is written in it "the inheritance of two tribes" — which implies that we institute a remedy for the mother's inheritance as well, that it not be transferred further. And this is the explanation of the Baraita: Behold, it says "And every daughter who inherits an inheritance," and the verse is speaking of a transfer through the husband, for a remedy is effective for the mother's inheritance. And if you say that it speaks of a transfer through the son, and the verse comes to institute a remedy only for the father's inheritance — come hear: "No inheritance shall be transferred," and from the redundancy of the verses we learn that one is about a transfer through the son and one about a transfer through the husband. And if so, that [verse] in which "the inheritance of two tribes" is written, which implies that a remedy is required for the mother's inheritance — it is written about a transfer through the husband, for in that case we find a remedy.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:11:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רב פפא לאביי דלמא שאני התם שכבר הוסבה - אע"ג דכתיב ביה "ירושת שני מטות", לא קפיד קרא אנחלת האם שכבר הוסבה, ולעולם קאי בסיבת הבן, אע"ג דליכא תקנתא לנחלת האם. א"ל: "שכבר הוסבה" לא אמרינן. אין סברא לומר שלא הקפיד הכתוב אנחלת אם אע"פ שכבר הוסבה, דכיון דכתיב "ירושת שני מטות", משמע דבנחלת האם עבדינן נמי תקנתא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:11:1.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye: Perhaps it is different there, since she already was married off - Even though it is written regarding it, "the inheritance of two tribes," the verse was not concerned about the inheritance of the mother, since she had already been married off; and [Rav Pappa maintains that] the verse still stands [concerned] with the reason of the son, even though there is no remedy for the mother's inheritance. [Abaye] said to him: We do not say "since she was already married off." It is not logical to say that the verse was not concerned about the mother's inheritance even though she had already been married off, for since it is written "the inheritance of two tribes," it implies that in the case of the mother's inheritance too we apply a remedy.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:12:1.hebrew: אמר ליה רב יימר לרב אשי אי אמרת בשלמא שכבר הוסבה היינו דמתוקמי קראי בין בסיבת הבן בין בסיבת הבעל כו' - רב יימר לא הוה יודע דאביי כי הוה מוקי לקרא בסיבת הבעל, מפרש לקרא דמנסבינן לה גברא דאבוהי משבטא דאבוה ואימיה משבטא דאימה. ולהכי קשיא ליה: אמאי ניחא ליה לאוקומי בסיבת הבעל טפי מבסיבת הבן? ובין הכי ובין הכי, כי מינסבא לשבטא דאבוה — מתעקרא נחלת האם משבטא דאימא לשבטא דאבא, כיון דלא אמר שכבר הוסבה. ומשני דמנסבינן לה וכו'. ועל פ"ה יש לתמוה, שאין זה שיטת גמרא: דרב פפא אקשי לאביי אברייתא, ואביי לא מהדר מידי, ועושה בעיא שלו בלשון קושיא. ועוד, דמסיק אביי "שכבר הוסבה לא אמרינן", ולפירושו הוה ליה למימר "ודלמא", דהא מספקא ליה, ואין בספרים "ודלמא". ועוד, דבכל הספרים גרסינן "אמר ליה אביי", דמשמע דאקושיא דאקשי ליה רב פפא מהדר לשנויי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:12:1.english: Rav Yemar said to Rav Ashi: "If you say, granted, that she was already transferred, that is why the verses are reconciled, both in the case of the son's cause and in the case of the husband's cause," etc. - Rav Yemar did not know that when Abaye established the verse as dealing with the husband's cause, he explained the verse as: we marry her to a man whose father is from her father's tribe and whose mother is from her mother's tribe. Therefore he found it difficult: Why is it preferable to him to establish it as the husband's cause rather than the son's cause? Either way, when she marries into her father's tribe, the mother's inheritance is transferred from the mother's tribe to the father's tribe, since he did not say that she was already transferred. And [Abaye] answers that we marry her, etc. But according to Rashi's commentary there is room for astonishment, for this is not the approach of the Gemara: Rav Papa challenged Abaye from the baraita, and Abaye does not answer anything, but rather makes his own inquiry in the form of a challenge. Furthermore, Abaye concludes, "We do not say that she was already transferred," whereas according to Rashi's explanation he should have said "perhaps," since he is uncertain about it, and in the texts there is no "perhaps." Furthermore, in all the texts we read "Abaye said to him," which implies that it is to the challenge that Rav Papa raised against him that he goes back to respond.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:1:1.hebrew: מנין ליאיר שלא היה לשגוב - תימה לרשב"א: אי לבאי הארץ נתחלקה הארץ, אמאי לא היה ליאיר שלא היה לשגוב:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:1:1.english: "From where [do we know] that Yair did not have [a portion] from Segub?" - The Rashba found this puzzling: If the land was divided among those who entered the land, why would Yair not have had [a portion], on the grounds that Segub had none?

Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:4:1.hebrew: וכי תימא לעבור עליו בשני לאוין - תימה: הא היכא דאיכא למידרש לא מוקמינן בלאוי יתירי! וכי תימא דהכי קאמר, דאפילו אי מוקמת להו בלאוי יתירי, איכא למילף שהבעל יורש את אשתו — דלא משמע הכי בסמוך, דקאמר: "לעולם קראי בסיבת הבן", כדשנינן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:4:1.english: "And if you say [that the verses come] to make him transgress two negative commandments" - This is puzzling: where there is something to derive through exposition, we do not establish [the verses] as superfluous negative commandments! And if you say that this is what [the Gemara] means — that even if you establish them as superfluous negative commandments, one can still learn [from them] that a husband inherits his wife — this is not implied by what [the Gemara] says right afterward, where it says: "Actually, the verses [refer] to the matter of the son [being the cause of the transfer]," as we answered.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:6:1.hebrew: אם כן תרי קראי למה לי - אע"ג דקרא קמא נמי שלא לצורך, דכבר שמעינן מתורת משה סיבת הבן, מ"מ בזה אינו מקפיד אי אשמועינן יהושע נמי סיבת הבן; אבל תרי זימני לית ליה לאשמועינן. רשב"א:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:6:1.english: "If so, why do I need two verses?" - Even though the first verse too is not needed [for this purpose], since we already learned the matter of sibbat haben (the transfer of inheritance from tribe to tribe through a son) from the Torah of Moses, nevertheless in this regard [the Torah] is not particular if Joshua also teaches sibbat haben; but twice, it should not need to teach it. Rashba.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:9:1.hebrew: אימא דנפלה ליה משדה חרמים - תימה לרשב"א: דלמה דוחק כל כך? כיון דבעא למימר דאתא קרא להראות עשרם, הוה ליה למימר דפנחס ויאיר ירשו מאמם, או מאבי אמם:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 112a:9:1.english: "Say that it fell to him from a field of devoted property" - The Rashba found this puzzling: Why does [the Gemara] strain so much? Since it wanted to say that the verse came to show their wealth, it should have said that Pinchas and Yair inherited from their mothers, or from their mothers' fathers:
